end.summary:
Practised that a freely suspended magnet settles roughly north-south.
Practised using compass markings and an object’s position to identify directions.
Made a simple compass by rubbing a clip with a magnet; linked its action to Earth behaving like a giant magnet.
Mahi corrected the idea that cold air makes a compass point north.
Teach-back was not passed; east/west and turning directions needed review.
end.parentNote: Mahi practised finding north-south with a magnet, reading compass directions, and making a simple compass. They used the explanation that Earth behaves like a giant magnet and corrected the mix-up about cold air causing the compass direction. They also connected a rubbed clip with a compass needle, though east/west and left-right turns were still mixed up at times. At home, practise with a compass by facing north and saying which side is east and which side is west.
